findings.title: Merged matrix artifacts cannot provide the aggregate job with three distinct cache receipts
evidence: .github/workflows/external-oss-v6-dependency-cache.yml:379-387 uploads cache-receipt.json and diagnostics.json from each task-specific directory. Under upload-artifact's documented least-common-ancestor rule, each artifact therefore contains the same two root-relative names.
.github/workflows/external-oss-v6-dependency-cache.yml:396-401 downloads all three receipt artifacts to one path with merge-multiple: true.
.github/workflows/external-oss-v6-dependency-cache.yml:410-413 recursively selects cache-receipt.json files, then requires receipts.length === 3 and the exact three task IDs.

actions/upload-artifact@v4 documentation states that the least common ancestor of multiple input paths is the artifact root: https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02/README.md#L187-L189

actions/download-artifact@v4 documents that merge-multiple true extracts matched artifacts into the same destination, and its implementation passes the same resolvedPath to every download: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093/README.md#L71-L75 and https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/blob/d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093/src/download-artifact.ts#L172-L181

The independent path-cardinality check derived root-relative names [cache-receipt.json, diagnostics.json] for every task and one distinct merged cache-receipt path versus the aggregate requirement of three.
findings.impact: All three task receipts target the same destination pathname during the merged download. Whether extraction overwrites/races on that path or fails on the collision, the aggregate directory cannot contain three distinct cache-receipt.json paths, so the required aggregate-cache-qualification job cannot satisfy its cardinality gate or produce a valid READY qualification.
findings.requiredRepair: Keep artifacts separated by removing merge-multiple: true (the existing recursive reader can then find one receipt under each artifact directory), or preserve a unique task-ID directory inside each artifact. Add a contract/regression assertion that the downloaded layout yields exactly three distinct receipt paths and exactly TASK-OSS-01, TASK-OSS-03, and TASK-OSS-09.

repairCriteria.result: The source cache is recursively made read-only before cache.tgz is archived and again after extraction in both diagnosis and offline verification. Only negative_cache receives chmod -R u+rwX before host rm; absence is asserted; negative_cache is restored with chmod -R a-w before its read-only mount. The committed contract test uses cache_root/negative_cache and checks the key writable-removal-readonly order in both blocks; an independent full-sequence assertion also checked extraction, source readonly, absence, and mount order. No chmod 777/0777 exists.

The harness maps both missing and existing-but-unreadable required cache entries to DEPENDENCY_CACHE_INCOMPLETE. The regression creates a mode-000 existing entry and asserts that exact code; a separate Bash access check confirmed the entry existed but was unreadable and mapped to DEPENDENCY_CACHE_INCOMPLETE.

The regression table-drives TASK-OSS-01/node_modules, TASK-OSS-03/node_modules, and TASK-OSS-09/.venv/bin/python, requires nonzero rm under a read-only parent, and requires the target to remain. A separate temp-only reproduction observed rm exit 1 and targetRemains=true for all three cases.

The EXIT trap extracts only one of nine whitelisted structured codes from captured positive/negative output and otherwise writes the fixed OFFLINE_PERMISSION_CAUSE_UNKNOWN fallback. Executing the extracted function returned HOME_NOT_WRITABLE for a specific-code sample and the fixed fallback for unknown raw text, without copying raw text into the result.
